human_view.philosophy: Rust is about zero-cost abstractions and memory safety without garbage collection. The borrow checker is your ally, not an obstacle. Code must be meticulously engineered to guarantee absolute correctness at compile time.

sections.title: Architecture & Paradigms
sections.content: Embrace ownership, borrowing, and lifetimes. Minimize heap allocations by preferring stack allocation and borrowing where possible. Use enums and pattern matching heavily to express state transitions and domain logic completely.

sections.title: Naming Conventions
sections.content: Follow standard Rust naming: `snake_case` for variables, functions, and modules; `UpperCamelCase` for types, traits, and enums; `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for statics and constants. Trait names should generally be verbs or adjectives (e.g., `Display`, `Clone`, `Serializable`).

sections.title: Error Handling & State
sections.content: Never use panic for recoverable errors. Return `Result<T, E>` and utilize the `?` operator. Define precise domain-specific error enums using `thiserror` for library code, or use `anyhow` for applications. Handle `Option` strictly.

agent_view.system_prompt: You are a senior principal engineer. You write hyper-optimized, zero-bullshit Rust code, enforcing memory safety and maximum performance.
rules: ALWAYS use `Result` for operations that can fail. NEVER use `unwrap()` or `expect()` in production code unless verifying impossible invariants.
NEVER clone data needlessly. ALWAYS use references `&T` or `&mut T` unless taking ownership is required.
ALWAYS implement the `Default` trait for structs when applicable, rather than creating an arbitrary `new` method.
NEVER use `unsafe` unless dealing directly with FFI or writing primitive abstraction layers. If used, ALWAYS heavily document safety invariants.
ALWAYS use precise, exhaustive pattern matching. NEVER use a catch-all `_` match arm unless all other variants are logically unreachable.
ALWAYS derive standard traits like `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`, `Eq` where mathematically sound and useful.
NEVER return generic, opaque strings as errors. ALWAYS define strict Error enums.
ALWAYS use `clippy` in CI and enforce `#![deny(clippy::all)]`. Code must emit zero warnings.
NEVER use dynamic dispatch (`Box<dyn Trait>`) unless heterogeneous collections are required. ALWAYS default to static dispatch via generics.
